title: Code Reviewer operator API, version 1
description: The wire format of the operator API (#275, #278, #284): a machine interface for an operator who sets the entitlements of workspaces, reads what they consumed and redeems the handover of a workspace Owner or Admin, from outside the app. Every request carries 'Authorization: Bearer <OPERATOR_API_TOKEN>'; a request body is application/json up to 16384 bytes, and GET and DELETE carry none. Every answer is JSON with 'Cache-Control: no-store' and the version in its body; an error is {version, error, field?} with a stable code, never a message. Until OPERATOR_API_TOKEN is set the paths do not exist (the 404 of a missing path, not this format). The API identifies workspaces by id and slug only: no names of people, no emails, no repositories, no pull requests. A reader ignores fields it does not know. This file is the only source of the format; the app tests validate real answers and contracts/examples/operator-api holds one valid example per definition.

Version.description: The version of the format; also in the path (/api/operator/v1).

WorkspaceId.description: The id of a workspace, as listed by GET /workspaces.

ApiErrorCode.description: Callers branch on the code. 401 unauthorized; 404 not_found (unknown path) or workspace_not_found; 405 method_not_allowed (with an Allow header); 400 body_not_allowed (a GET or DELETE with a body), request_invalid (not JSON, or a bad query such as a limit out of range), cursor_invalid (a usage cursor that is not one of the API's) or period_invalid (a usage 'from' or 'to' that is not a timestamp, a period that is empty, or a summary without both); 413 body_too_large; 415 unsupported_media_type; 409 period_start_backwards; 422 the other codes of a refused entitlement, among them cost_limit_requires_managed_key for a cost limit next to keyMode 'own' (the codes of the workspace entitlements validation, with 'field' naming the limit or key concerned); 422 also invalid_token (a handoff token that is unknown, used, expired, revoked or whose person lost the role: one answer for all) and the codes of a refused plan management address (url_invalid, url_not_https, url_has_credentials, url_has_fragment, url_too_long); 500 internal_error.

field.description: For a refused entitlement: the limit or the unknown key concerned (never its value).

EntitlementLimits.description: Every limit is required on a write; null is unlimited.

diffRunsPerPeriod.description: A count (or micro-USD of measured model cost) per period, or null for unlimited.

dynamicRunsPerPeriod.description: A count (or micro-USD of measured model cost) per period, or null for unlimited.

managedCostLimitMicroUsd.description: A count (or micro-USD of measured model cost) per period, or null for unlimited.

EntitlementLimitsWrite.description: The limits of a write: every limit, and no other key (a typo is refused with limits_invalid).

diffRunsPerPeriod.description: A count (or micro-USD of measured model cost) per period, or null for unlimited.

dynamicRunsPerPeriod.description: A count (or micro-USD of measured model cost) per period, or null for unlimited.

managedCostLimitMicroUsd.description: A count (or micro-USD of measured model cost) per period, or null for unlimited.

EntitlementsFields.description: What an operator allows a workspace, as read back.

planLabel.description: A label for display and audit, 1 to 64 printable characters. The app never branches on it.

keyMode.description: Whose LLM key the workspace's reviews use. 'managed' is the operator's key.

suspensionCode.description: Why the workspace is suspended: lowercase letters, digits, '_' and '-', starting with a letter, at most 64 characters. null unless suspended.

EntitlementsWrite.description: The body of PUT /workspaces/{id}/entitlements and PUT /entitlements/default: the whole entitlements, replacing what was stored. Unknown keys are refused (a typo must not pass). 'periodStart' may be left out: the stored start is kept, or the period starts now when nothing is stored. A start earlier than the stored one is refused (period_start_backwards, 409) and one more than five minutes ahead as period_start_in_future. A write is idempotent. A numeric limit above 2^53-1 is refused (limit_invalid) instead of being rounded. Removing a workspace's row (DELETE) ends the 'never backwards' guard for that workspace: a later PUT without periodStart begins now. A cost limit (managedCostLimitMicroUsd, even 0) next to keyMode 'own' is refused (cost_limit_requires_managed_key): it only counts runs on the operator's key, so it would never be read. An entry of that shape that was stored earlier keeps working: it is read as before and the limit is ignored.

planLabel.description: A label for display and audit, 1 to 64 printable characters. The app never branches on it.

keyMode.description: Whose LLM key the workspace's reviews use. 'managed' is the operator's key.

suspensionCode.description: Why the workspace is suspended: lowercase letters, digits, '_' and '-', starting with a letter, at most 64 characters. null unless suspended.

InvalidEntitlements.description: A stored entry that cannot be read. It counts as 'invalid' for enforcement (fail closed); a valid PUT repairs it.

StoredEntitlements.description: The row of a workspace, with the time of its last write. Who wrote it is not part of the format.

EffectiveEntitlements.description: What applies to the workspace on its next claim: its own row, else the default, else nothing (unlimited: own key, no limits, not suspended). A running job is not touched.

EntitlementsSource.description: 'workspace': the workspace's own row. 'default': the instance default.

WorkspaceList.description: GET /workspaces?after=<id>&limit=<1..200, default 50>: workspaces ordered by id after the cursor. 'nextAfter' is the id to pass as 'after' for the next page, null on the last page.

WorkspaceEntitlementsResponse.description: The answer of GET, PUT and DELETE /workspaces/{id}/entitlements: the stored row (null when none, e.g. after DELETE) and the effective entitlements.

DefaultEntitlementsResponse.description: The answer of GET and PUT /entitlements/default: the default for workspaces without a row, an invalid marker for damaged data, or null when none was set. The default cannot be removed through the API.

UsageCursor.description: An opaque position in the usage feed: keep the 'nextCursor' of an answer and pass it back as 'after'. Do not parse it or build one; one the API did not write is refused with cursor_invalid. At most 128 characters of base64url.

UsageReason.description: Why a record carries no measurement, as a short code (lowercase letters, digits and '_'), or null. A reader ignores a code it does not know. 'no_result': the job ended without any result from the runner that held it (it died, its lease ran out on the last attempt, it ran past the hard limit), so the model may have been used and the cost and the tokens are unknown. A run that reported its usage, failed or not, carries no reason; an unpriced run has a null cost and its tokens.

UsageItem.description: One settled run. Nothing about the pull request, the repository, the branch, the title or any person is in it, and 'modelTier' is the name of a quality tier, never the name of a model. 'costMicroUsd' is millionths of a US dollar of measured model cost, null when the run could not be measured (never a guess); the token counts are null when unknown. A record is immutable once it is served.

id.description: The id of the record: the idempotency key. A reader that is handed a record twice (it retried a page) keeps one.

jobId.description: The id of the review job the record belongs to; one record per job.

keyMode.description: Whose LLM key the run used. 'managed' is the operator's key.

modelTier.description: The quality tier of a managed run, or null. Only a tier name is ever shown (lowercase letters, digits, '_' and '-', starting with a letter, at most 32 characters); anything else is served as null.

UsagePage.description: GET /usage?after=<cursor>&limit=<1..200, default 50> (every workspace) and GET /workspaces/{id}/usage?after=&limit=&from=&to= (one workspace; 'from' included and 'to' excluded, on 'settledAt'): a page of SETTLED records ordered by (settledAt, id) after the cursor. Records that are reserved or void are never served. A record is served only once its 'settledAt' is more than 60 seconds old (the safety lag), so a record that commits late cannot appear behind a position a reader already holds; a reader that polls therefore sees the newest minute of settlements a little later. 'nextCursor' is the position after the last item, or the cursor that was passed when the page is empty, or null when nothing has been served and none was passed: keep it and pass it as 'after' next time. Treat 'id' as the idempotency key: keep one item per id, however often a page is read.

UsageSummaryGroup.description: What one workspace ran in the period, for one kind of review and one key mode. 'recordCount' counts the runs that count towards a limit (running or settled; void runs are left out), 'settledCount' those among them that are settled, 'knownCostMicroUsd' adds up the cost of the settled runs whose cost is known, and 'unknownCostCount' counts the settled runs whose cost is not known (they add nothing to the sum).

UsageSummaryResponse.description: GET /workspaces/{id}/usage/summary?from=&to=: both are required timestamps with 'from' before 'to'. A run belongs to the period it started in ('from' included, 'to' excluded), the same rule the limits count by, so this summary is what a limit sees; it is not a view of the feed (which is by time of settlement) and a run still in progress is counted in 'recordCount'. The groups are ordered by review kind then key mode; a combination without runs is not listed. The summary counts by the time a run started ('reserved_at'), so it does not reconcile with the feed, which is by time of settlement, at the edges of a period (a run that started on the 30th and settled on the 1st is in the earlier period's summary and the later period's feed). A closed period's counts can still change until its last run has ended: 'recordCount' minus 'settledCount' is the number still in progress. For accounts by time of settlement, use the feed.

PlanManagementWrite.description: The body of PUT /plan-management: the address of the page a workspace Owner or Admin is handed over to when they click 'Manage plan' in the app. It has to be an absolute https address without user name, password or fragment; it is stored in its normal form. Anything else is refused with 422 and one of the url_* codes. Unknown keys are refused (400 request_invalid).

PlanManagementResponse.description: The answer of GET, PUT and DELETE /plan-management: the address in its stored form, or null while there is none. While there is none, the app shows no 'Manage plan' button and its route does not exist. The app appends the single query parameter 'handoff=<token>' to this address when it hands somebody over (any 'handoff' parameter in the stored address is replaced); the page that receives it redeems the token at once with POST /handoff/redeem and does not keep it in its address bar, its logs or its links.

HandoffRedeemRequest.description: The body of POST /handoff/redeem: the token from the 'handoff' query parameter. Exactly this key. A token of any other shape is not a request error: it gets the same invalid_token answer as an unknown one.

HandoffRedeemResponse.description: The answer of POST /handoff/redeem for a valid token: which workspace the person who clicked 'Manage plan' belongs to and with which role. A token is valid for five minutes after the click and works once; a newer click of the same person in the same workspace revokes it; the role is checked again at redemption (a person who is no longer a member with the role the token was made for gets invalid_token, and the token is used up). 'userId' is opaque: the same person always has the same id, and it is nothing an email, a name or a repository could be recovered from. Nothing else about the person is ever served. The service redeems the token before it shows anything, and sends the person back to /w/<workspaceSlug>/settings of the app (until the plan page of #282 exists; it will then be /w/<workspaceSlug>/settings/plan); that path is fixed on the app's side.
